title: Extend policy engine with burst guardrail rules (max ratio, cooldown, global fleet caps)
author: Jordan Lee
description:
Context: Dedicated burst capacity needs guardrails that are (a) configurable, (b) deterministic, and (c) explainable. Admission Controller and Routing both consume the policy engine for decisions, so we need first-class rule support rather than ad-hoc config parsing.

This PR adds a BurstGuardrailsV1 rule set to the policy engine bundle to express:
- per-tenant max_burst_ratio (e.g., 1.5x baseline)
- per-tenant burst cooldown window (min seconds between allowed burst intervals)
- per-region/hardware global fleet safety caps (absolute + percentage) and an optional emergency disable bit

The goal is to make guardrails expressible entirely via policy bundle config (with defaults), while keeping evaluation deterministic under telemetry lag. This PR DOES NOT change admission behavior by itself; it extends the policy engine schema + evaluation result so downstream services (admission controller, router) can rely on a stable contract.

Key decisions/semantics:
- Determinism: evaluation is a pure function of (request context, tenant config, policy bundle, fleet snapshot metadata). This PR defines which fleet fields are allowed inputs and forces explicit snapshot_ts propagation.
- Cooldown is evaluated using a monotonic server time provided in the context (now_ms) plus a stable last_burst_admitted_ms in the tenant runtime state passed to the policy engine. No lookups inside the policy engine.
- Max burst ratio is expressed against tenant reserved_baseline_gpus (or reserved_capacity_units); if missing, policy returns a validation error and defaults to deny-burst (fail closed).
- Global caps can be expressed per (region, hardware_class) with an override wildcard ("*") entry.

Implementation overview:
- Adds new policy schema types in policy/guardrails/burst_guardrails_v1.{go,proto}
- Adds bundle validation with clear error messages (surfaced to control plane on publish)
- Adds evaluation output: burst_guardrails_decision { allowed_max_burst_units, cooldown_remaining_ms, global_cap_remaining_units, deny_reason_code }
- Adds unit tests + golden tests for common configurations and edge cases
- Adds minimal docs/comments in policy bundle examples

Testing:
- Unit tests for parsing/validation
- Golden tests for evaluation determinism
- Fuzz test for schema decode + unknown fields handling

Follow-ups:
- Admission controller will consume burst_guardrails_decision (ENG-4810) and wire last_burst_admitted_ms + fleet snapshot inputs
- Routing will consume deny reason + recommended backoff when denied (ENG-4812)

Refs:
- ENG-4821 Guardrails: cooldown + fairness enforcement
- ENG-4902 Fleet safety cap and global circuit breaker

Risk: low-to-medium. Changes are gated to the new rule name (BurstGuardrailsV1). Existing bundles are unaffected unless they opt in.

Release note: none (internal contract change; feature still behind flags).

tests: golden tests for ratio/cooldown/global cap combinations

conversation:
Ethan Park (review): Can we make sure cooldown uses the same notion of time as admission controller? We’ve been burned by mixed wall/mono time in past rate limiters.

Jordan Lee (author): Yep — I changed context to require now_ms (provided by caller) and disallowed any internal time.Now() usage in the guardrails evaluator. Added a test that fails if evaluator touches system time (via a fake clock that panics).

Keiko Yamamoto (review): For global caps, can we support a wildcard default per region? Some regions will not have per-HW overrides at launch.

Jordan Lee (author): Added resolution order: exact (region, hw) -> (region, "*") -> ("*", "*"). Validation enforces at least a ("*", "*") entry if rule is enabled so we don’t end up with implicit infinity.

Sean Gallagher (review): Please ensure fail-closed behavior is explicit for missing baseline fields. I’d rather deny burst than guess.

Jordan Lee (author): Agreed. Validation error on publish, and evaluation returns deny_reason_code=POLICY_INVALID_CONFIG if baseline missing. Downstream can surface this as "misconfigured" rather than "capacity".

Mina Haddad (review): Router needs deterministic deny codes for retries/backoff. Are we locking down reason codes here?

Jordan Lee (author): Added enum-like string constants in policy/guardrails/deny_reason_codes.go and tests. Codes included: COOLDOWN_ACTIVE, TENANT_CAP_REACHED, GLOBAL_CAP_REACHED, FLEET_SAFETY_DISABLED, POLICY_INVALID_CONFIG.

Benji Okafor (review): Can we keep the policy output small? We don’t want to explode label cardinality if people start emitting these fields as metrics.

Jordan Lee (author): Output is intentionally compact (ints + a single deny code). Also added guidance in docs to avoid emitting raw tenant ids with deny codes.

Ethan Park (approval): Looks good. Please add one more golden case for the wildcard cap resolution and I’m good.

Jordan Lee (author): Added golden test `wildcard_resolution_region_default`.

Keiko Yamamoto (approval): Approved.

Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved; thanks for the explicit fail-closed behavior.
merge_outcome: Merged into main; rollout remains behind feature flags (no behavior change until admission controller consumes the new rule).
